es: Reconocer los cuatro ganchos de apertura (pregunta, anécdota, dato y promesa) y las señales que anuncian la estructura de una charla.

teaching.en: A strong opening grabs the audience with a hook in ten seconds.

teaching.en: She began with an anecdote: last year she lost her suitcase in Rome.

teaching.en: Her promise was simple: by the end, you will know how to open a talk.

teaching.en: Let me outline the talk: first the problem, then the solution.

es: Ordenar y completar un discurso con señales de organización (first, moreover, having said that, to sum up) y preguntas retóricas.

teaching.en: First, I will explain the problem; moreover, I will show you a solution.

teaching.audioText: Having said that, let me briefly turn to the risks.

prompt.es: Escribe el centro de una charla con inversión, regla de tres y pregunta retórica.

answer.text: Every night, millions of us do the same thing. We lie in bed, we pick up the phone, and we say, just five more minutes. But who has ever stopped after five minutes? Nobody. Never have we had so many tools to talk to each other, yet rarely do we feel rested. Not only do we lose sleep, but we also lose focus, energy and patience. Think about your last bad day at work or school. Was it the lack of ideas? Or was it the lack of sleep? Here is what I suggest: a simple plan with three rules. First, leave the phone outside your bedroom. Second, turn off the screen one hour before bed. Third, read a book instead. Little did I know that three small rules would change my mornings. Seldom have I felt so calm and so awake. So tonight, try it. Put your phone down, close your eyes and give your body the rest it needs.

First, leave the phone outside your bedroom. Second, turn off the screen one hour before bed. Third, read a book instead. Little did I know that three small rules would change my mornings. Seldom have I felt so calm and so awake. So tonight, try it. Put your phone down, close your eyes and give your body the rest it needs.

Every evening, most of us repeat the same habit. We take the phone to bed and we scroll for one more minute. Why do we do it? Because it feels harmless. Never have we been so connected, yet rarely do we feel calm. Not only does the screen steal our sleep, but it also steals our focus, our energy and our patience. So I suggest three simple rules. First, charge the phone in the kitchen. Second, switch off the screen an hour before bed. Third, read a few pages of a book. Seldom have I slept so well as in the week I tried it. prompt.es: Escribe tu charla de cinco minutos: gancho, tres ideas, cierre y respuesta.

answer.text: Have you ever run so slowly that a walker passed you? That was me, three years ago, on my first morning with the Park Runners club. I was a beginner, I was out of breath, and I wanted to quit. Today I will tell you why I stayed. First, running is not about speed; it is about habit. Moreover, the club gave me friends who waited for me at every corner. Having said that, nobody made me feel small. Second, running changed my head: I am calmer, happier and more patient. Seldom have I felt so proud as on the day I finished my first ten kilometres. Third, it is cheap. You only need shoes and a park. To sum up, run slowly, run with friends and never stop trying. That is my takeaway. And remember the walker who passed me? Last week, I passed him. Thank you for your question: you asked whether you must be fast to join. Not at all; beginners are the heart of our club.
accepted: Have you ever run so slowly that a walker passed you? That was me, three years ago, on my first morning with the Park Runners club. Moreover, the club gave me friends who waited for me at every corner. Having said that, nobody made me feel small. Second, running changed my head: I am calmer, happier and more patient. Seldom have I felt so proud as on the day I finished my first ten kilometres. Third, it is cheap. You only need shoes and a park. To sum up, run slowly, run with friends and never stop trying. That is my takeaway. And remember the walker who passed me? Last week, I passed him. Thank you for your question: you asked whether you must be fast to join. Not at all; beginners are the heart of our club.

Good evening. Nine out of ten people quit a new sport in the first month. Today I want to show you how to stay. First, choose a sport that you love. Moreover, find a club, because friends make every hour easier. Having said that, you must be patient. Second, practise a little every day. Third, enjoy the small wins. Never have I felt so happy as on the day I finished my first race. Last year, I was a beginner too, and I was afraid of looking silly. Now I look forward to every training. Why wait? Start this week, and you will see. To sum up, be patient, be kind to yourself and have fun. That is my takeaway. Good question, by the way: you asked if it is expensive. Not at all; a pair of shoes is enough.
